pll1d1c1-vanspv.summary: Programmatic opening: careful study of the Old and New Law reveals, by God's grace, that the treatment of sacred Scripture turns chiefly on things or signs.
claims: The content of Scripture concerns principally things or signs.

pll1d1c1-ueeeis.summary: Grounds the opening thesis in Augustine's division of all teaching into teaching about things and teaching about signs, and supplies the definitions: things are not used to signify, signs are those whose use is in signifying.
claims: All teaching is either of things or of signs.
Signs are things whose use lies in signifying.

pll1d1c1-eaases.summary: Divides signs into those whose whole use is to signify (certain sacraments of the Law) and those that both signify and confer inward help (the Gospel sacraments), anticipating Book IV.
claims: Some signs only signify and do not justify, such as legal sacraments.
Gospel sacraments signify and confer what inwardly helps.

pll1d1c1-eqadta.summary: Clarifies the relation of signs to things with Augustine: every sign is some thing, but not every thing is a sign. Concludes that a studious and modest theological inquiry will find that Scripture keeps this prescribed form of teaching.
claims: Every sign is a thing, since what is no thing is nothing.
Not every thing is a sign.
Scripture follows the form of teaching by things and signs.

pll1d1c1-dhedsd.summary: States the plan of the work: to open access to understanding divine things by discussing first things, then signs.
claims: The treatise will treat first of things and afterwards of signs.

pl-l1d1c1.summary: Opens the entire Sentences by setting its organizing principle: following Augustine's De doctrina christiana, all teaching concerns things (res) or signs (signa), with signs being things used to signify. Distinguishes merely signifying sacraments (legal) from those that also confer grace (evangelical), and announces the plan of the work: first things, then signs.
claims: Sacred Scripture is chiefly concerned with things and signs.
Every sign is a thing, but not every thing is a sign.
Some sacraments only signify (those of the Law); others signify and confer inward help (those of the Gospel).
The treatise will proceed first concerning things, then concerning signs.
concepts: sacraments of the Old and New Law
